title: Electric-Car Pioneer Elon Musk Charges Head-On at Detroit
summary: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla Motors, is making a significant push in the electric vehicle market, aiming to sell 500,000 vehicles annually by 2020. His return to Detroit for a public appearance highlights the increasing competition with traditional automakers, notably General Motors, which showcased a new electric car at the Detroit auto show. Tesla's stock market value has grown sixfold in the past two years, underscoring its rising prominence in the industry.

title: JetBlue to link Reno, New York City with daily flights
summary: JetBlue Airways announced new daily nonstop flights linking Reno with John F. Kennedy International Airport starting May 28, marking the first-ever daily direct service between the two cities. This new route is anticipated to be a "game changer" for Reno's economy, boosting tourism, economic development, and business travel by providing direct access to the lucrative New York market. JetBlue also plans to offer competitive fares, with promotional one-way tickets starting at $89.

title: Blog recap: Tesla exec Elon Musk speaks in Detroit
summary: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla, is speaking at the Automotive News World Congress in Detroit, two years after his last visit to the city. Tesla Motors has seen significant growth in that time, leading one analyst to call it "the world's most important car company." Freep reporters will be live blogging the event from the North American International Auto Show.

title: Tesla stock plunges after it posts $108-million quarterly loss
summary: Tesla Motors Inc. reported a significant loss of $107.6 million in the fourth quarter and $294 million for the full year, despite a 56% increase in quarterly revenue, due to heavy investments in new models and factories. CEO Elon Musk attributed the losses to a "delivery shortfall" caused by severe weather, shipping problems, and development glitches. Analysts expressed concerns as Tesla missed investor expectations, leading to a drop in its stock price.

title: Tesla Motors Inc. (TSLA) Is Sinking After Unexpected Q4 Loss
summary: Tesla Motors Inc. (TSLA) reported an unexpected adjusted loss of $0.13 per share for the fourth quarter, contrasting with a profit of $0.33 per share in the previous year and analyst expectations of $0.31. This news led to a sharp decline in the stock price, which dropped 16.80 to $196.00 on above-average volume, reaching a two-week low.

title: Tesla Motors Nearly Doubled Staff In 2014
summary: Tesla Motors nearly doubled its staff in 2014, growing from 5,859 to 10,161 employees, as it pursued ambitious global growth targets of 500,000 sales in a few years from 33,000 in 2014. This surge in hiring led to significant increases in selling, general, and administrative expenses, which more than doubled, and a substantial rise in research and development spending.

title: Apple’s new electric car could give Tesla a run for its money
summary: Apple Inc. is reportedly developing an electric car, codenamed "Titan," which could significantly increase competition in the electric vehicle market, especially for Tesla Motors Inc. While Apple has released no details on design or pricing, its entry is expected to make electric cars more mainstream and could prompt Tesla to accelerate its own developments. Despite potential competition, Tesla CEO Elon Musk has historically welcomed new entrants, believing it expands the overall market for electric vehicles.

title: Tesla Motors Stock Price: Volatile, but a Long-Term Win
summary: This article discusses the volatile nature of Tesla Motors Inc. stock (TSLA) but argues for its strong long-term potential due to its disruptive technology and ambitious projects like the Gigafactory and home batteries. Despite short-term fluctuations and analyst "Underperform" ratings, experts believe Tesla is a game-changer in both the auto and energy sectors, making it a compelling investment for patient investors. The stock's potential for significant growth is hinged on its ability to drive down battery costs and expand into new markets beyond luxury vehicles.

title: NVIDIA CEO Talks Titan X, Next-Gen Pascal, Deep Learning And Elon Musk At GTC 2015
summary: NVIDIA CEO Jen-Hsun Huang's GTC 2015 keynote covered deep learning, the GeForce GTX Titan X's launch at $999, and upcoming Pascal GPU architecture features like 3D-stacked memory and NVLink. The presentation also highlighted the Digits DevBox and included a discussion with Tesla CEO Elon Musk on autonomous vehicles and AI.

title: Tesla CEO Elon Musk and Nvidia CEO Jen-Hsun Huang declare self-driving cars “solved”
summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk and Nvidia CEO Jen-Hsun Huang discussed the future of self-driving cars at the 2015 GPU Technology Conference. Musk stated that autonomous driving is a "solved problem" and addressed the challenges in urban environments and the lengthy transition period for the automotive industry. Huang highlighted Nvidia's new technologies like Titan X and Drive PX, emphasizing the car as a "software computer on wheels."

title: Elon Musk Predicts Human Drivers Will Be Outlawed in the Future
summary: Elon Musk predicted that human drivers could be outlawed in the future due to the safety risks posed by human-operated vehicles, referring to cars as "two-ton death machines." He later clarified on Twitter that Tesla is strongly in favor of people being allowed to drive their cars. The article also discusses Tesla's Autopilot system and a concept Musk proposed to accelerate the deployment of autonomous cars by having them operate passively in the background to gather data.

title: Tesla Model X: Not a model launch
summary: The Tesla Model X, originally unveiled in 2012, has faced numerous delays, attributed primarily to its unique "falcon-wing" doors and CEO Elon Musk's pursuit of perfection. This article details the timeline of these delays, from initial launch targets in late 2013 to a revised summer 2015 delivery estimate. The ambitious design choices and their impact on the production schedule are highlighted, with the success of the launch dependent on overcoming these challenges.

title: Tesla to Upgrade Cars Through the Internet
summary: Tesla is positioning itself as a software company by committing to deliver a series of upgrades for its Model S electric cars directly to owners via the Internet within the next 10 days. These upgrades, rolled out over several months, will include features enabling complete autonomy on highways. This approach contrasts with the traditional auto industry's dealer-based upgrade model, as Telsa aims to cut out the middleman by using its cars' embedded wireless connections.

title: Elon Musk: Model S not a car but a ‘sophisticated computer on wheels’
summary: Elon Musk emphasizes that the Tesla Model S should be viewed as a "sophisticated computer on wheels" rather than just a car, highlighting Tesla's nature as a software company as much as a hardware company. The article discusses Tesla's ability to remotely update its vehicles with new features like automatic braking and partial autopilot, transforming how cars can evolve post-purchase. This approach contrasts with traditional car manufacturing where features are fixed at the time of sale, making the Model S more akin to a smartphone in its capacity for continuous improvement through software updates.

title: What Tesla Has the Technology to Produce -- Other Than Cars
summary: Tesla Motors is set to unveil a new product category on April 30 that is not a car, leading to speculation about what it could be. Analysts suggest the new product might be a battery for homes or an enhancement for existing Tesla vehicles, leveraging the company's Gigafactory. This announcement caused Tesla's stock to jump 3 percent.

title: Tesla blocked in W.Va. as governor signs bill
summary: West Virginia's governor has signed a bill blocking Tesla from directly selling its vehicles in the state. This move prevents Tesla from bypassing traditional franchised dealerships, a model it uses in other states. The legislation reflects ongoing tensions between direct-sales manufacturers and dealer associations.

title: Tesla Revs up Price, Power, Range of Model S
summary: Tesla has released an updated version of its Model S sedan, the 70D, which boasts increased range, power, and a higher starting price of $75,000. Despite the price hike, analysts like Jack Nerad from Kelley Blue Book believe the enhanced technology, particularly the extended range, makes it a worthwhile upgrade. Elon Musk notes that tax credits and fuel savings can significantly reduce the effective cost of the vehicle.

title: Elon Musk almost sold Tesla to Google, book claims
summary: A forthcoming book reveals that Tesla Motors Inc. was in such severe financial distress in early 2013 that Elon Musk nearly sold the company to Google Inc. This information challenges what was publicly known about Tesla's situation at the time. The claim is presented as a "surprise" within the book.

title: Tesla Website, Twitter Account, Musk Twitter Briefly Hacked
summary: The Tesla Motors website and official Twitter account, along with CEO Elon Musk's Twitter account, were briefly hacked on a Saturday afternoon. The hackers changed the account name, posted a phone number for a "free car," and included "shoutouts" to random accounts. Tesla had not yet responded to Green Car Reports' inquiry regarding the security breach, which occurred despite Tesla having a "Security Vulnerability Reporting Policy" on its site.

title: Hackers hijack Tesla's website, Twitter account and email - but how?
summary: Hackers successfully hijacked Tesla's website, official Twitter account, and CEO Elon Musk's personal Twitter account, displaying prank messages and advertising a fake giveaway. The article explains that the hackers achieved this not by breaching Tesla's servers directly, but by altering DNS records and potentially MX mail server records, which allowed them to redirect web traffic and intercept password reset emails for Twitter accounts. This incident highlights the importance of two-factor authentication and the vulnerabilities associated with DNS and email server record management.

title: Tesla CEO Plugs Into New Market with Home Battery System
summary: Elon Musk has unveiled the "Powerwall" home battery system, aiming to revolutionize energy use by allowing homes to disconnect from traditional power plants. While initially expensive, Tesla hopes to sell billions of these battery packs globally, reducing reliance on fossil fuels and creating decentralized power networks. The system also targets commercial and utility markets, with major companies like Amazon.com and Target planning to use Tesla's battery storage.

title: Tesla moves into batteries that store energy for homes, businesses
summary: Tesla Motors Inc. unveiled Tesla Energy, a new business venture focused on storage systems or batteries for homes, businesses, and utilities, expanding beyond electric vehicles. CEO Elon Musk aims to fundamentally change energy consumption on a large scale. The company introduced Powerwall for homes and a larger power pack for utilities, anticipating profitability in the battery product segment.

title: Did Tesla nearly go bankrupt without investors knowing?
summary: A new biography of Elon Musk suggests that Tesla Motors was on the brink of bankruptcy in early 2013 and that Musk approached Google for a potential acquisition. This near-collapse went unnoticed by investors and analysts, with a surge in Model S sales ultimately saving the company. The article explores how such a critical financial situation could remain hidden from the public and financial observers.

title: SolarEdge to provide inverter technology for Tesla’s solar-powered Powerwall battery
summary: SolarEdge, an Israeli company, is set to provide inverter technology for Tesla's new solar-powered Powerwall battery. This collaboration will integrate SolarEdge's optimized inverter solutions with Tesla's energy storage system, marking a significant step in residential solar energy solutions.

title: Tesla buys Grand Rapids auto supplier, its first presence in Michigan
summary: Tesla Motors has acquired Grand Rapids-based auto supplier Riviera Tool, marking its first manufacturing presence in Michigan. This acquisition is crucial for Tesla to expand production of its Model S and upcoming Model X vehicles, and the company plans to retain Riviera's 100 employees and rename it Tesla Tool & Die. The move comes as Tesla faces pressure to ramp up production and after Michigan signed a law preventing direct sales of Tesla vehicles to consumers in the state.

title: Elon Musk: Demand for Tesla’s home battery is ‘crazy off the hook’
summary: Elon Musk has stated that demand for Tesla's Powerwall home batteries is "crazy off the hook," with 38,000 pre-orders already received, far exceeding current production capacity. Tesla expects to be sold out through mid-next year and is considering boosting capacity at its "gigafactory." The company also launched the larger Powerpack for commercial use and utilities, for which 2,500 units have been pre-ordered.

title: Mint.com Founder on What It's Like to Be an Employee at Your Own Company (Hint: It Stinks)
summary: Mint.com founder Aaron Patzer shares his experiences after selling his startup to Intuit for $170 million, detailing the challenges of being an employee in his former company and navigating leadership changes. He discusses past failures, his new venture Fountain, and offers advice to entrepreneurs on solving their own problems and being fully committed.

title: Tesla acquires Michigan-based auto supplier
summary: Tesla Motors Inc. has acquired Riviera Tool, LLC, a Michigan-based tool and die manufacturer, which will be renamed Tesla Tool and Die Factory. This acquisition aims to streamline production and facilitate the introduction of the Model X, marking Tesla's first presence in Michigan. The move is seen as a strategic step for Tesla to expand its in-house manufacturing capabilities and meet its ambitious production goals.

title: Tesla 'supercharger' station in Salina one of only 3 in New York
summary: A new Tesla Motors Inc. "supercharger" station has opened in Salina, New York, making it one of only three in the state and 425 worldwide. The station allows Tesla owners to charge their electric cars in about 45 minutes for free, a significant improvement over standard charging times. This new infrastructure supports long-distance travel for Tesla owners, as demonstrated by a family traveling from Canada to Cape Cod.

title: SolarEdge to debut new PV storage for residential at #IntersolarEurope
summary: SolarEdge is set to introduce its new StorEdge DC-coupled PV storage solution for residential systems at Intersolar EU, which includes an inverter solution compatible with both grid and Tesla's Powerwall. The company will also reveal expanded commercial solutions with new 25kW, 27.6kW, and 33.3kW inverters designed to improve system ROI. These new offerings underscore SolarEdge's commitment to lowering solar energy costs and accelerating PV adoption globally.

title: Remember Solyndra? Tesla just leased the defunct solar panel maker’s old space
summary: Tesla Motors has leased a 500,000-square-foot facility at 901 Page Ave. that previously housed Solyndra, the bankrupt solar panel manufacturer. This new space is located less than three miles from Tesla's Fremont factory and will provide additional room for manufacturing and engineering labs, signaling the company's continued expansion beyond its main factory. The move highlights Tesla's need for more space despite already possessing a massive former auto plant and acquiring other facilities for parts production.

title: This Is the Perfect Tesla Supercharger Roadtrip
summary: A data scientist named Mortada Mehyar used a sophisticated algorithmic approach to solve the "traveling salesman problem" for Tesla's Supercharger stations, aiming to find the shortest route to visit all of them in the U.S. His method, using a program called Concorde, efficiently identified an optimal path for the 194 Superchargers available at the time, providing a solution to a complex logistical challenge for electric vehicle owners. The article notes that the number of Superchargers had already grown to 196 by the time of publication, highlighting Tesla's rapid expansion.

title: Early Tesla Motors Investors Raise $400 Million Impact VC Fund
summary: Early investors in Tesla Motors Inc., Nancy Pfund and Ira Ehrenpreis, have collaboratively launched a new $400 million venture capital fund. This fund is dedicated to investing in startups that aim to create positive social or environmental impacts. The initiative is part of the San Francisco-based venture firm, DBL Partners.

title: Walmart and Tesla have a lot in common when it comes to taxes
summary: This article examines the unexpected similarities between Walmart and Tesla, particularly focusing on their business strategies, environmental impact, and tax practices. It highlights how both companies, despite their different industries, have faced scrutiny over tax avoidance, government incentives, and their environmental claims. The author argues for greater transparency in company disclosures regarding government support and tax contributions.

title: GE engineer is a prolific inventor
summary: Ajith Kumar, a consulting engineer at GE Transportation, holds 256 U.S. patents and many more internationally, making him GE's most prolific inventor worldwide. He is particularly proud of innovations like a dynamic weight management locomotive and a system that significantly reduces fuel consumption in trains. Kumar attributes his success to a constant drive to solve problems with commercial value for GE, inspired by inventors like Thomas Edison and Nikola Tesla.

title: Linde wind plant a necessary step in creating hydrogen-fueled cars
summary: Linde has opened a plant that uses wind power to convert water into hydrogen, aiming to make hydrogen-fueled cars a viable alternative to battery-electric vehicles. This development, alongside Toyota's Mirai production and a standardized refueling network across Germany, addresses the three critical steps for hydrogen car adoption: generation, refueling, and vehicles. The article highlights the advantages of hydrogen cars, such as faster refueling and longer ranges, while acknowledging cost and infrastructure challenges.

title: Tesla Motors upgrades the Model S with ‘ludicrous mode’
summary: Tesla Motors has introduced new updates for its Model S electric sedan, including a "ludicrous mode" that accelerates the car from 0 to 60 mph in 2.8 seconds and a larger battery option. CEO Elon Musk also announced a lower-priced Model S and progress on upcoming models like the Model X SUV, Model 3, and a new Roadster. These enhancements aim to extend performance, range, and affordability for Tesla customers.

title: Tesla Adds ‘Ludicrous Mode’ for Drivers With Need for Speed
summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced new options for the Model S sedan, including a "Ludicrous Mode" for enhanced speed, a battery upgrade to 90 kWh for extended range, and a new cheaper base model. The battery upgrade costs $3,000 and adds 15 miles of range, while the new base model with rear-wheel drive is priced at $70,000. These updates cater to various driver preferences, from speed enthusiasts to those seeking more affordable or longer-range options.

title: Tesla’s Musk: New ‘ludicrous’ mode shoots Model S to 60 mph in 2.8 seconds
summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced several new options for the Model S, including a "ludicrous" driving mode that allows the car to go from 0 to 60 mph in 2.8 seconds. The company also introduced a new base model, a more powerful battery pack, and announced updated timelines for the Model X and Model 3. While analysts noted the improvements would generate consumer interest, they emphasized that Tesla's future hinges on the successful launch of its new models and increasing sales volume.

title: eBay Inc. CFO Bob Swan Wins Lifetime Achievement Award
summary: eBay Inc. Senior Vice President and CFO Bob Swan received a Lifetime Achievement Award at the Bay Area CFO of the Year Awards in 2014. Swan expressed his surprise and humility, attributing his success to unique opportunities and supportive colleagues. The event also honored CFOs from Tesla Motors and Wikimedia Foundation and raised over $467,000 for Larkin Street Youth Services.

title: Dow Jones Industrial Average Today Drops 180 Points as IBM, UTX Slide
summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 180 points or 1% on July 21, 2015, primarily due to significant slides in IBM and United Technologies Corp. shares following weak revenue figures and a slashed profit outlook, respectively. Other market movers included a drop in Verizon Communications, marginal gains in oil prices, and upcoming earnings reports from major companies like Apple and Microsoft, while specific stocks like Tesla and Lexmark also experienced notable declines.

title: What Tesla is doing in America’s newest smokestacks-free manufacturing city
summary: This article highlights how former industrial towns, specifically Fremont, California, and the Sheffield urban area in the U.K., are transforming into "innovation districts." These districts foster advanced manufacturing by co-locating large companies like Tesla (TSLA) with startups, research institutions, and urban amenities, moving beyond the traditional image of manufacturing. The success of these hardware-software hubs is crucial for modern economies, contributing significantly to GDP and providing high-paying jobs.

title: Infographic: Tesla Motors Powering a Sustainable Future
summary: This article discusses the projected demand for lithium, graphite, and cobalt for Tesla Motors' gigafactory, according to Benchmark Mineral Intelligence. Tesla's facility is expected to require significant amounts of these metals by 2020, representing substantial percentages of 2014 global supply. The article highlights that this demand, coupled with other megafactories, will necessitate fundamental changes in upstream markets for these critical metals.

title: Tesla burns cash, loses more than $4,000 on every car sold
summary: Tesla Motors is reportedly losing over $4,000 on every Model S electric sedan sold and burned $359 million in cash last quarter. CEO Elon Musk is considering options to raise more capital, including selling more stock, as the company targets mass production and expansion into electric power storage systems. Analysts express concerns over the cash burn rate and the company's capital spending projections given its ambitious expansion plans.

title: Elon Musk Is About To Make A Huge Investment In Tesla
summary: Tesla Motors is planning to raise approximately $500 million through a stock offering of 2.1 million additional shares, with CEO Elon Musk indicating he will invest about $20 million. The proceeds will fund the development of the more affordable Model 3 sedan, expand retail operations, and boost charging stations and battery factory development. This investment comes as Tesla reported a net loss of $184 million in the second quarter.

title: Crane accident cuts electricity to Tesla Motors Fremont factory
summary: A crane accident on Friday morning cut power to Tesla Motors' factory in Fremont, California, forcing the plant to shut down. The incident, which occurred at 6:35 a.m., involved a power line running into the factory. PG&E is currently on-site to address the situation, and power is expected to be restored soon with no injuries reported.

title: Elon Musk’s Brave New World: it worked for Henry Ford; why not Tesla?
summary: This article compares Tesla's strategy under Elon Musk to Henry Ford's approach with the Model T, focusing on vertical integration and mass-market affordability. It explores how Ford's standardization enabled low prices and wide adoption, and how Tesla aims to achieve similar success with electric vehicles by controlling battery production and targeting a lower price point. The author also discusses the evolving role of supply chain management and technology in enabling greater variety and innovation while maintaining cost efficiency, offering advice to Tesla based on Ford's successes and limitations.

title: The most hyped emerging technology of 2015
summary: Gartner Inc.'s Hype Cycle of Emerging Technologies report identifies autonomous vehicles as the most hyped technology of 2015, alongside the Internet of Things. Despite significant media attention and technological advancements, Gartner warns of unrealistic expectations, stating that fully autonomous vehicles are still 5-10 years away from mainstream adoption due to cost, legal, and ethical challenges. The report predicts a phased approach to driverless cars and anticipates massive shifts in industries like auto sales when the technology matures.

title: Tesla Named World's Most Innovative Company by Forbes
summary: Forbes has named Tesla Motors the world's most innovative company for the first time, ranking it number one on its fifth annual list. This marks a shift from Salesforce.com, which had held the top spot for five years. The rankings are based on analysis from Finstra Consulting and Innovators DNA, utilizing a proprietary valuation model from HOLT.

title: The $132,000 'Signature Series' Tesla Model X has arrived
summary: Tesla is preparing to deliver its "Signature Series" Model X SUV, priced at $132,000 before incentives, in late September. These top-tier models come with a 90 kWh battery, Autopilot, and the option for "Ludicrous Mode" for an extra $10,000. While the initial models are expensive, regular production-run Model X SUVs are expected to be priced significantly lower, and the release is an important step for Tesla as it moves towards its mass-market Model 3.

title: Tesla's Model 3 to Cost $35K in March, But Production Still 2 Years Away
summary: Tesla's Model 3 is set to cost $35,000 and has a debut plan for March, as announced by Elon Musk. However, the mass-market car is not expected to arrive until 2017 at the earliest, largely due to the need for the Gigafactory to produce more affordable batteries. In the interim, the Model X is expected to begin production on September 29.

title: Five cars that make the Tesla Model X look like a deal
summary: This article discusses the high price point of Tesla Motors Inc.'s new Model X, specifically the "Signature" version, which costs $134,000, with an additional $10,000 for the "ludicrous" performance package. It highlights that the first Model X vehicles are set to roll out from Tesla's Fremont, Calif. factory on September 29, as announced by CEO Elon Musk. The title suggests that despite these prices, there are other cars that make the Model X seem like a good value.

title: Understanding Tesla Motors’s Product Portfolio
summary: This article examines Tesla's product portfolio, focusing on the currently available Model-S and the upcoming Model-X, expected later in 2015. It also mentions the highly anticipated mass-market Model-3, which is still a few years away. The author highlights Tesla's success in building a strong brand and compares its products to Apple's in terms of customer enthusiasm, while noting the ultimate key to success will be a mass-market electric vehicle.

title: Tesla Motors Inc.'s Big Bet on Model X in 2 Charts
summary: This article examines Tesla Motors' significant investment in its Model X SUV, which is projected to double the company's sales. Through two charts, the author illustrates Tesla's ambitious sales targets and expected accelerated growth trajectory. The Model X aims to tap into the large SUV market, potentially reaching 79,000 deliveries within its first four full quarters of availability.

title: Tesla Signs Another Supply Agreement With Pure Energy Minerals
summary: Pure Energy Minerals announced a lithium supply agreement with Tesla Motors, marking the second such agreement for the automaker in recent weeks. Under the deal, Pure Energy will potentially supply lithium hydroxide from its Clayton Valley project in Nevada to Tesla, with Tesla committing to annual purchases over five years at a predetermined price. This agreement validates Pure Energy’s project and contributes to Nevada's clean energy economy, though pricing and delivery details remain confidential.

title: It’s official: Tesla’s Model X launch event is the night of September 29
summary: Tesla has officially announced its Model X launch event for the evening of September 29th at its Fremont, California factory. This event is a critical moment for Tesla as it aims to demonstrate its ability to produce another successful vehicle following the Model S and meet its end-of-quarter delivery deadline for the first Model X cars. The company plans to deliver between 50,000 and 55,000 cars in total for 2015, including both Model X and Model S vehicles, with Model X production ramping up in the fourth quarter.

title: Why the Model X is so important for Tesla
summary: Tesla's Model X launch event marks a significant transition for the company, moving beyond the highly successful Model S to offer multiple products and attract new customer demographics. The Model X is crucial for Tesla to meet its annual shipment goals and generate revenue for future projects like the cheaper Model 3 and its grid battery business, despite facing production challenges and delays. The success of the Model X will be a key indicator of Tesla's ability to scale production and realize its ambitious growth targets.

title: Is Goldman Sachs’ Gary Cohn Ready to Step in for Lloyd Blankfein?
summary: This article examines Goldman Sachs President Gary Cohn's readiness to potentially succeed CEO Lloyd Blankfein, especially after Blankfein's recent lymphoma diagnosis. It highlights Cohn's transformation from an impatient executive to a more polished and visible leader, who has gained significant experience and acceptance within the firm. The piece suggests that Blankfein's health news puts a brighter spotlight on Cohn's evolving role and increased suitability for the top position.

title: Tesla's first SUV, the Model X, is finally hitting the road
summary: Tesla officially unveiled its first SUV, the all-electric Model X, which features unique falcon-wing doors and advanced technology. The Model X aims to attract new customers, especially women, to the brand in the booming luxury SUV market, despite a high price point. Tesla expects half of its sales to be SUVs and plans for a less expensive Model 3 by 2017 to reach its goal of 500,000 vehicles sold by 2020.

title: Tesla’s First SUV, the Model X, Is Finally Hitting the Road
summary: Tesla officially unveiled its first SUV, the Model X, delivering the initial six vehicles to buyers. CEO Elon Musk highlighted its unique features like falcon-wing doors and a self-closing driver's door, positioning it to attract new customers, particularly women, in the booming luxury SUV market. Despite its high price point ($142,000 for a fully loaded model, around $93,000 for the base), the Model X, sharing a platform with the Model S and featuring a 90 kWh battery, is key to Tesla's goal of selling 500,000 vehicles by 2020.

title: Tesla Unveils Model X, an All-electric SUV
summary: Tesla officially unveiled its all-electric SUV, the Model X, targeting the booming luxury SUV market and aiming to attract new customers, especially women. CEO Elon Musk highlighted its unique features like falcon-wing doors and advanced engineering, despite acknowledging the vehicle's complexity and high price, with a fully loaded model costing $142,000. The Model X is a crucial step for Tesla, which expects SUVs to constitute half of its sales, and it faces competition from other automakers planning their own electric SUVs.

title: See the Coolest Features of Tesla’s Newest Car
summary: The Tesla Model X, released on September 30, 2015, is the company's first SUV. Key features include Falcon Wing doors, a 250-mile electric range, expansive trunk space, touchscreen controls with an optional 'bioweapon defense mode' filtration system, and a 5,000-pound towing capacity.

title: 4 things to know about Tesla’s Model X
summary: This article announces the imminent rollout of Tesla's all-electric Model X vehicles from its Fremont, California factory. It highlights the SUV's performance capabilities, specifically mentioning its 0-60 mph acceleration in 3.2 seconds. The piece notes that the Model X is launching after experiencing previous delays.

title: Google Co-Founder Sergey Brin Said to Get Tesla's Fourth Model X
summary: Google co-founder Sergey Brin, an early investor in Tesla Motors Inc., was reportedly one of the first customers to receive Tesla's all-electric Model X SUV. Tesla CEO Elon Musk handed over the first six vehicles at an event in Fremont, California, with Musk keeping the first and venture capitalist Steve Jurvetson receiving the second.

title: General Motors plans drive into autonomous cars
summary: General Motors announced plans to unveil a self-driving Chevy Volt next year, signalling a major push into autonomous vehicle technology and a strategic shift to compete with companies like Tesla and Google. The initiative involves partnerships with firms such as Mobileye and will be partly funded by a cost-cutting plan. GM also revealed plans to develop ride-sharing technologies, aiming for a city-wide program in 2016, and addressed concerns about diesel car emissions.

title: Bioweapons Experts Seriously Doubt Tesla's New Apocalypse Mode
summary: Tesla's new Model X features a "bioweapon defense mode" with a medical-grade HEPA filter, activated by a button for apocalyptic scenarios. However, experts and Gizmodo report that while the filter is effective against large bacteria, some viruses like smallpox and influenza could still penetrate it. Additionally, the lack of clear signs for bioweapon attacks makes timely activation of the mode improbable.

title: Known Tesla bulls sound the alarm about Model X price
summary: Analyst bulls at Morgan Stanley have expressed concerns that the high price of Tesla's newly released Model X SUV could hinder the company's ability to meet its sales targets. Consequently, they have lowered their price target on Tesla's stock to $450 from $465, though this revised target is still significantly higher than the average analyst target. The report highlights that despite the Model X's engineering achievements, its cost is a potential barrier to widespread adoption and sales success.

title: Sorry, but the Model X isn’t meant to save the world
summary: The Tesla Model X is positioned as a way for Tesla to generate additional revenue and demonstrate its ability to produce multiple vehicle types, not as a low-cost electric car for the masses. The article emphasizes that the Model X is an evolutionary step for the company, leveraging technology from the Model S, while the more affordable Model 3 remains the true path to mainstream electric vehicles, dependent on the Gigafactory's completion. The Model X aims to attract new customers and provide financial stability until the Model 3 becomes available.

title: Barra: GM will lead self-driving revolution
summary: GM CEO Mary Barra states that General Motors is among the leaders in self-driving car development, despite competition from Silicon Valley giants like Apple and Google, and electric-vehicle maker Tesla Motors. She emphasizes GM's commitment to innovation, including the development of the "Super Cruise" system and an affordable long-range electric car, while navigating the shifting automotive landscape and addressing investor concerns. Barra also discusses GM's stance on mergers, its relationship with regulatory bodies, and the broader challenges and opportunities in the evolving auto industry.

title: The Hipster Hardware Store That Has Home Depot Scared
summary: TreeHouse, an eco-conscious home-improvement store in Austin, Texas, is challenging big-box retailers like Home Depot by focusing on sustainable design, smart-home technology, and a highly curated showroom experience. Founded by Jason Ballard, the company aims to be a multibillion-dollar business by making green home solutions accessible and competitive in price. Despite early struggles and personal hardships, Ballard's vision and persistence led to significant growth and partnerships with brands like Nest and Tesla.

title: Top 10 CEOs of Automotive World
summary: This article lists the top 10 CEOs who have significantly impacted the automotive industry by driving growth and innovation, even during challenging times. It highlights leaders like Mary Barra of General Motors, Elon Musk of Tesla Motors, and Carlos Ghosn of Renault-Nissan Alliance, detailing their achievements and contributions. The list also includes figures from traditional automakers and disruptive forces like Google, showcasing the diverse leadership shaping the future of the auto world.

title: Tesla to host grand opening of its Burbank showroom
summary: Tesla opened a new showroom and service center in Burbank, California, on October 23, 2015, marking a significant expansion for the electric car manufacturer in the Los Angeles area. The new facility allows customers to customize and order Tesla vehicles, with plans to include superchargers and an owners' lounge. City officials and Tesla executives highlight the location's importance for promoting electric vehicle adoption and catering to a tech-savvy clientele in the entertainment industry.

title: Tesla Motors opens local showroom
summary: Tesla Motors has opened a new showroom and service center in Burbank, California, offering customers a personalized experience to design their electric vehicles and featuring advanced car capabilities like "ludicrous mode" and autopilot. The new location aims to serve a growing base of Tesla owners in the Los Angeles area, particularly studio executives and entertainment industry professionals. This expansion is significant for Burbank, aligning with the city's embrace of electric vehicle technology through the installation of new charging stations.

title: Tesla Gets Boost From Korean Battery Maker LG Chem
summary: Tesla Motors Inc. confirmed a contract with South Korean battery maker LG Chem Ltd. for upgrades to its original Roadster vehicle. This partnership enables Tesla to offer a $29,000 battery replacement and other improvements to Roadster customers, significantly increasing the car's range to around 400 miles. This collaboration highlights Tesla's commitment to enhancing its older models and utilizing advanced battery technology.

title: Nvidia’s CEO, Jen-Hsun Huang, Receives a Brand New Tesla Model X P90D – Congratulates Elon Musk and Nvidia’s Team
summary: Nvidia's CEO, Jen-Hsun Huang, received a new Tesla Model X P90D, likely as a recognition of Nvidia's crucial role as a supplier for Tesla Motors, powering its digital cockpit system with Tegra chips. This event highlights the strong partnership between Nvidia and Tesla, particularly as Tesla moves towards autonomous vehicles, with Nvidia's Drive PX and Drive CX chips expected to play an increasingly significant role. Huang publicly congratulated Elon Musk and both the Tesla and Nvidia teams, emphasizing the increasing importance of Nvidia's technology in autonomous driving.

title: Why Elon Musk's Tesla is losing its luster
summary: This article discusses the growing skepticism surrounding Tesla as it approaches its Q3 earnings report, highlighting concerns from auto executives and analysts about the company's financial health, manufacturing challenges, and market strategy. Critics point to cash burn, build quality issues, and the capital-intensive direct sales model as potential hurdles for the electric car maker, despite its success in making EVs aspirational.

title: Tesla Misses In Q3 Earnings, With Adjusted Revenue Of $1.24 Billion And A Drop $.058 In EPS
summary: Tesla reported Q3 earnings that missed analyst expectations, with adjusted revenue of $1.24 billion and a non-GAAP loss per share of $0.58. The company produced 13,091 cars and delivered 11,603 in Q3 2015, leading to a lowered full-year sales guidance. Tesla plans to invest $500 million in Q4 to speed up Gigafactory production, particularly for the Model X, and expects improved Model X gross margin in Q1 2016 after initial launch expenses.

title: Tesla gigafactory construction, production ahead of schedule
summary: Tesla's Reno, NV, gigafactory construction and battery cell production for Tesla Energy products are ahead of schedule, with cell production now expected to begin by the end of next year. Tesla has also moved production of its Powerwall to an automated line within the new facility. The "$5 billion Nevada gigafactory could become the world’s largest building in terms of footprint by the time it is finished."

title: Gartner: 21 Billion IoT Devices To Invade By 2020
summary: Gartner predicts an explosion in the Internet of Things (IoT) market, with nearly 21 billion connected devices expected by 2020. While consumer devices will account for the greatest number, enterprises will drive the largest spending on IoT, with services expected to reach $235 billion in 2016. The report highlights the growing importance of IoT and its impact on IT within businesses.

title: Gigafactory lands on Tesla’s fast track to Big Battery era
summary: This article details Tesla's ambitious Gigafactory project in Nevada, a $5 billion, 10-million-square-foot plant aimed at mass-producing lithium-ion batteries to significantly reduce costs and support the widespread adoption of electric cars and renewable energy storage. The Gigafactory, built in partnership with Panasonic, is critical for Tesla to meet its projected production goals and solidify its position as a major manufacturer, facing both significant opportunities and risks in a rapidly evolving market. The article also touches on the intense bidding war between states for the factory, with Nevada ultimately securing the project through a substantial tax incentive package.

title: Can Tesla’s enthusiast customers help it sell the electric car for the everyperson?
summary: This article explores how Tesla's enthusiastic early adopters, like "Darrell," are crucial to its initial success but questions if their fervor can translate to the mass market for the upcoming Model 3. It delves into the challenges Tesla faces in affordability, customer service scalability, and managing the "elephant in the room" – battery degradation and replacement costs, which could hinder its transition to a broader consumer base.

title: Entry-level Tesla Model X 70 priced from $80,000
summary: Tesla announced an entry-level Model X 70D, priced from $80,000, catering to a broader market beyond the initial high-end P90D deliveries. The 70D features a 70 kilowatt-hour battery, a 220-mile range, and a 0-60 mph time of 6.0 seconds. This move positions the Model X against future rivals, with deliveries of the 70D expected later in 2016.

title: Custom Tesla Model X Thanks Company's Veterans, Model S Too
summary: Tesla Motors has created custom Model X and Model S vehicles in military trim to promote its veteran recruitment efforts. These unique vehicles appear at public events to draw attention to Tesla's interest in hiring veterans for their technical skills, integrity, and discipline. The company reports that veterans now constitute 6 percent of its U.S. employee population.

title: Why a Vermont Utility is Selling Tesla Batteries
summary: Green Mountain Power, a Vermont utility, is the first U.S. utility to sell Tesla batteries to its customers, allowing homeowners to access backup power or pair them with solar panels. This move is unusual given the small and over-hyped U.S. home battery market, but is driven by Green Mountain Power's progressive leadership, Vermont's need for backup power during harsh storm seasons, and the utility's smart home initiatives. The utility aims to integrate these batteries to make the grid and homes smarter, offering customers reduced costs if they share battery control.

title: More Bad News for the Tesla Model S
summary: A survey by Plug-In America revealed that nearly two-thirds of early production Tesla Model S sedans experience battery component failure before 60,000 miles, impacting over 200 drivetrains. This issue, along with a "worse-than-average overall problem rate" cited by Consumer Reports, raises reliability concerns despite Tesla's 97% customer satisfaction and generous eight-year warranty. Consumers appear willing to overlook these problems for the car's superior range, performance, and advanced technology.

title: Tesla: We’re Sticking With Mobileye Car Tech
summary: Tesla Motors announced its commitment to continue using Mobileye's driver-assistance technology, refuting industry speculation and stock price fluctuations based on rumors of a switch to technology developed by George Hotz. Tesla spokesman Ricardo Reyes debunked Hotz's claims about a proposed contract and challenged the feasibility of a small company developing a production-ready autonomous driving system. The company clarified that Mobileye's technology is an important, but not sole, component of its Autopilot system, which also integrates radar, ultrasonics, GPS, and cameras, and constantly learns from its entire fleet.

title: Tesla Starts Shipping “Signature Series” Model X Cars To Customers
summary: Tesla has begun delivering its "Signature Series" Model X crossover SUVs to customers who placed early deposits, with prices ranging from $132,000 to $144,000. The company has produced "hundreds" of Model X vehicles and plans to start shipping "general production" versions soon, which are expected to cost at least $70,000. CEO Elon Musk aims to increase Model X production to several hundred vehicles per week by year-end, despite potential technical and logistical challenges.
